title.zh: 环形线圈 Green 场响应

summary: Evaluate the closed-form psi, BR, and BZ response of aligned circular coils from caller-supplied elliptic values.

identity.direction: regularized observation geometry and coil vectors to summed flux and fields
identity.definition: Apply the scalar closed-form Green expressions to aligned coil arrays and sum the per-coil terms.
identity.model: Closed-form axisymmetric circular-coil response using supplied K(m) and E(m).
identity.geometry: One observation point paired with one-dimensional coil arrays.
identity.coordinates: R,Z in metres; current amperes; turns count; psi Wb/rad and fields tesla.
identity.boundary: Observation on a source ring is singular and rejected; the observation-radius offset is not repeated.
assumptions: All coil vectors are finite one-dimensional arrays with matching shapes.
Supplied elliptic values correspond to the supplied modulus values.

inputs.name: regularized_radius_m
inputs.description: Observation radius after the source axis offset (from the coil Green geometry operator).
inputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive; the offset is applied once by the caller and is not repeated here.

inputs.name: coil_radius_m
inputs.constraints: Finite 1-D, strictly positive entries, shared shape with the other coil vectors.

inputs.name: modulus_squared
inputs.description: Per-coil squared elliptic modulus m = k^2.
inputs.constraints: Finite; entries in (0, 1) after singular rejection; exactly 1 marks an observation point on a filament ring and is rejected.

inputs.name: complete_k
inputs.description: Per-coil first-kind complete elliptic integral K(m).
inputs.constraints: Finite where modulus != 1 (the singular-geometry rejection makes non-finite pairings unreachable on accepted inputs).

inputs.name: complete_e
inputs.description: Per-coil second-kind complete elliptic integral E(m).

outputs.name: flux_weber
outputs.description: Total poloidal-flux response psi = R A_phi summed over coils.
outputs.units: Wb/rad (per the psi = R A_phi convention; subject to the caller's current units)
outputs.constraints: Finite on accepted inputs; overflow from finite but extreme currents/turns raises ValueError (declared hardening).

outputs.name: radial_field_t
outputs.description: Total radial field response B_r summed over coils.
outputs.constraints: Finite on accepted inputs; overflow from finite but extreme currents/turns raises ValueError (declared hardening).

outputs.name: axial_field_t
outputs.description: Total axial field response B_z summed over coils.
outputs.constraints: Finite on accepted inputs; overflow from finite but extreme currents/turns raises ValueError (declared hardening).

preconditions: All coil vectors are finite one-dimensional arrays with matching shapes.
supported: Finite aligned coil arrays, current linearity, mirrored-pair cancellation, and singular/overflow failures in direct tests.
excluded: Misaligned coil geometry, internally recomputing elliptic integrals, and arbitrary extreme-scale guarantees.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: ValueError is raised for malformed vectors, invalid modulus/elliptic values, singular geometry, or nonfinite output.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Arithmetic overflow and invalid closed-form operations are converted to ValueError.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; the response is a finite direct sum.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No scalar tuple is returned after validation or singularity failure.

python.signature: evaluate_filament_coil_green_field(regularized_radius_m, observation_z_m, coil_radius_m, coil_z_m, current_a, turns, modulus_squared, complete_k, complete_e)

example.description: Evaluate a mirrored pair of coils and repeat with doubled current.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.field import (
    compute_axisymmetric_coil_modulus,
    evaluate_complete_elliptic_integrals,
    evaluate_filament_coil_green_field,
)
radius, modulus, _ = compute_axisymmetric_coil_modulus(
    0.3, 0.0, np.array([0.2, 0.2]), np.array([-0.1, 0.1]))
k, e = evaluate_complete_elliptic_integrals(modulus)
flux, br, bz = evaluate_filament_coil_green_field(
    radius, 0.0, np.array([0.2, 0.2]), np.array([-0.1, 0.1]),
    np.array([10.0, 10.0]), np.array([2.0, 2.0]), modulus, k, e)
assert abs(br) < 1e-18
flux2, br2, bz2 = evaluate_filament_coil_green_field(
    radius, 0.0, np.array([0.2, 0.2]), np.array([-0.1, 0.1]),
    np.array([20.0, 20.0]), np.array([2.0, 2.0]), modulus, k, e)
assert flux2 == 2.0 * flux and bz2 == 2.0 * bz
example.expected: The mirrored pair cancels BR on the midplane; doubling current doubles all three scalar responses; a singular ring raises ValueError.

scope: Closed-form responses against an independent recomputation.
Cross-implementation agreement with the baseline scipy-elliptic filament relation at equal elliptic values.
Singular-geometry rejection and input failure contracts.
verification.evidence_ceiling: The direct tests establish the three responses against an independent closed-form recomputation (exact float equality), linear superposition in current, midplane B_r cancellation of a mirrored pair, and the fail-closed input contracts including the singular-geometry rejection. With identical scipy-evaluated K and E the closed form agrees with the baseline scirel.field.circular-filament-green response to rtol 1e-12 on probed geometries (same physics, different arrangement); feeding the polynomial-log approximation instead shifts responses by up to ~1e-5 relative on the probed set, consistent with the approximation's documented ~1e-8 K/E error amplified by the closed form -- sampled evidence over probed geometries, not a continuous bound. No test establishes the responses against an external physics reference beyond the shared closed form.
known_limitations: No external cross-implementation comparison is bound to this contract; only the tests in this repository establish its behaviour.

This asset is a declared relation variant of scirel.field.circular-filament-green, not a new Green capability; the variant boundary (caller-supplied elliptic values, scalar target, source regularization, fail-closed singulars) must not be collapsed by silent unification.

Declared input hardening chain (documented for the family): the geometry operator rejects raw negative observation radii, and this operator rejects zero-separation/modulus-1 singular geometry; neither boundary is silently accepted here.
Declared output hardening: finite but extreme current/turns magnitudes that overflow the combined response factor raise ValueError instead of returning Inf/NaN.
The singular-geometry rejection (observation point on a filament ring) is an explicit contract: that configuration raises rather than returning NaN responses.
Public distribution licensing remains pending a human decision.
